doc_summary: The post presents three LLM-based alignment auditing agents (investigator, evaluation, breadth-first red-teaming) validated on target models with researcher-implanted behaviors that provide ground truth. It discusses scalability and validation challenges, and limitations such as dev/test contamination and the unrepresentativeness of artificial implanted behaviors.

items.claim: prefers validating auditing methods on models with known, implanted issues over relying on unvalidated audits because ground truth lets you measure coverage and answer 'did we catch everything?'.
items.quote: Did our audit catch everything? How can we rule out that models have substantive issues not surfaced by alignment audits? In our paper Auditing Language Models for Hidden Objectives (Marks et al., 2025), we proposed auditing games as a validation protocol

items.claim: Distrusts results from implanted-behavior testbeds as proxies for real model behavior, since artificial quirks may be unrepresentative of naturally arising misalignment.
items.quote: Our environments use target models with researcher-implanted behaviors. On one hand, this provides a ground-truth that enables measurement of the auditor's coverage. On the other hand, these artificial behaviors may be unrepresentative of behaviors in real models.

items.claim: Distrusts headline performance numbers when the same environment served for development and testing, flagging dev/test contamination as undermining representativeness.
items.quote: We use the auditing game environment from Marks et al. as both a test environment and a development environment for eliciting agent capabilities. While we took measures to avoid overfitting (discussed below), this nevertheless represents a form of dev/test contamination

items.claim: prefers running many parallel agents from identical initial states over single human-auditor runs because it gives replicable, statistically meaningful comparisons of tools and affordances.
items.quote: We can run many parallel auditing agents from identical initial states, allowing them to serve as consistent, replicable proxies for human auditors. Crucially, this enables fine-grained analysis of auditing methodologies

items.claim: For open-ended elicitation, use breadth-first probing with hundreds of parallel conversations to surface unspecified concerning behaviors, accepting that a human must review many transcripts.
items.quote: in order to achieve this, the agent conducts a broad investigation to produce many potentially-concerning transcripts which a human must review.

items.claim: Read agent failure as fixation on early hypotheses and mitigate by aggregating many parallel runs in an outer loop rather than trusting a single trajectory.
items.quote: However, it struggles with fixating on early hypotheses. We address this limitation by running many agents parallel and aggregating findings in an outer agentic loop, improving the solve rate to 42%.

items.claim: Treats evals as convincing only if they discriminate models with versus without a known behavior, using this as the criterion for 'measures what it's supposed to'.
items.quote: successfully discriminates models with vs. without implanted test behaviors in 88% of runs. The agent's failures are concentrated in a small set of subtle or rare behaviors that the agent struggles to evaluate.

items.claim: Cautions that agent auditors fail in non-human ways (e.g. state-keeping), limiting the validity of agents as proxies for human auditors and the conclusions drawn about affordances.
items.quote: our agents also sometimes struggle in ways that a human wouldn't (e.g. with maintaining state over the course of a long investigation). This reduces their validity as a proxy for human auditors

items.claim: Chooses what to test by pairing realistic frontier-audit needs (sycophancy, alignment faking, hidden goals) with controlled testbeds, and validates agents under realistic conditions before real-world use.
items.quote: We additionally go beyond controlled research environments by using our agents for real-world auditing tasks.
